package_info.package_manager: Manual/Custom deployment (malware distributed via CI/CD compromise, not a public package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: GraphicalProton is a backdoor deployed by threat actors after exploiting JetBrains TeamCity and Zabbix vulnerabilities. It enables persistent remote access, data exfiltration, and command execution, leveraging trusted cloud services for stealthy command-and-control. Its deployment subverts the software supply chain, allowing attackers to manipulate builds and steal sensitive assets.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (post-exploitation, after initial access to TeamCity/Zabbix server)
execution_context.file_location: Hijacked Zabbix DLL (DLL side-loading in Zabbix installation directory)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious DLL loaded via DLL hijacking, replacing or masquerading as a legitimate Zabbix DLL. The DLL loads at Zabbix service start and executes embedded backdoor logic.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At service startup, the malicious DLL is loaded by the Zabbix process via DLL hijacking, establishing persistence and executing backdoor logic to enable remote command execution and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DLL hijacking is a classic technique for stealthy code execution and persistence, especially when a legitimate process loads an attacker-controlled DLL.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Zabbix DLLs should not contain backdoor logic or enable remote access. Loading untrusted DLLs from the application directory is abnormal.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: DLL side-loading is sometimes used for legitimate debugging or plugin extension, but not for backdoor deployment.
key_indicators: DLLs with network communication or process injection code

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after backdoor installation, on attacker command or scheduled interval)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Outbound HTTPS requests to OneDrive or other trusted cloud services, used as command-and-control (C2) channels for exfiltration and receiving attacker instructions.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During runtime, the backdoor establishes outbound HTTPS connections to attacker-controlled OneDrive accounts, polling for commands and exfiltrating collected data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of trusted cloud services for C2 is a stealthy evasion technique, blending malicious traffic with legitimate business activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Zabbix/TeamCity processes should not communicate with external cloud storage for command polling or data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated backup or sync tools may use cloud storage, but not for arbitrary command execution or exfiltration.
key_indicators: Unusual OneDrive/Dropbox/Google Drive traffic from server processes
Outbound connections to attacker-controlled cloud accounts

execution_context.file_location: Memory (injected or executed by attacker via backdoor)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Execution of Mimikatz or similar credential dumping tool to extract Windows credentials and password hashes from memory.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After gaining privileged access, the attacker executes Mimikatz to dump credentials from LSASS, enabling lateral movement and privilege escalation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Credential dumping is a hallmark of post-exploitation activity, used to expand attacker access within the network.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate processes should not access LSASS memory or extract credential material.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Forensic or incident response teams may use credential dumping tools in controlled investigations.
key_indicators: Unusual process injection or memory reads

attack_chain.action: Exploit CVE-2023-42793 in JetBrains TeamCity or Zabbix vulnerability to gain initial access to CI/CD or monitoring server.
Deploy GraphicalProton backdoor via DLL hijacking in Zabbix or direct installation on TeamCity server.
Establish outbound C2 channel using trusted cloud services (e.g., OneDrive) for command polling and data exfiltration.
Execute credential dumping tools (e.g., Mimikatz) to extract credentials and escalate privileges.
Use compromised CI/CD environment to manipulate builds, steal source code, signing certificates, or inject further malware into the software supply chain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Supply chain compromise and persistent access

behavioral_signatures: DLL hijacking in Zabbix or other monitoring tools
Outbound HTTPS traffic to cloud storage services from server processes
Execution of credential dumping tools (Mimikatz) on CI/CD or monitoring servers
Unusual process injection or memory access patterns
file_indicators: Unexpected DLLs in Zabbix or TeamCity directories
Modified or unsigned DLLs replacing legitimate binaries
Presence of Mimikatz or similar binaries
network_indicators: Outbound connections to OneDrive, Dropbox, or other cloud storage from CI/CD or monitoring servers
Unusual encrypted traffic to cloud services not associated with normal business operations
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized DLLs in application directories, especially those loaded by Zabbix or TeamCity processes. Alert on outbound HTTPS connections to cloud storage services from server infrastructure. Detect execution of credential dumping tools and access to LSASS memory. Correlate privilege escalation and lateral movement with recent software or DLL changes on critical infrastructure.
